rows: This was one of the worst severe episodes of the 2006 spring severe weather season. There were several long lived supercells that produced large hail swaths with hail sizes ranging up to baseball size hail that produced widespread damage across several West Central Texas towns or…
Penny size hail was reported about three miles west of Lohn on highway 504.

Skywarn storm spotters watched a landspout tornado develop and skip along the ground for several miles before lifting. The tornado moved across a rather remote area with only minor damage to wheat crops noted.
The land spout tornado touched ground once again. It remained over open fields with no damage reported.
A tornado crossed over from Menard County and remained in open fields.
Trees and road signs were blown down on Farm to Market Road 503 about 8 miles south of Doole.
There were several reports of large hail in the city. This hail was part of a 15 mile wide swath of hail that began near Melvin and continued along and south of U.S. Highway 87 to Brady.
A brief tornado was reported about a quarter mile east of Melvin.
A storm survey revealed that a tornado with winds between 65 and 85 mph caused damage to storage buildings, a marina, trees, and other vegetation along the southeast side of Brady Lake.

Before power was lost, a wind gust of 60 knots was reported at the Brady Airport AWOS. High winds knocked down trees, power lines and damaged about 100 businesses and homes in Brady including the civic center.
Quarter size hail was covering US-283 just east of Lohn.
Small tree limbs were blown down.
Quarter size hail was reported at the intersection of Highways 283 and 87.
A roof was blown off of a barn just west of Placid.
A part of a roof was blown of a house.
A roof was blown of a house in the southwest part of Brady.
Wind gusts of 50 mph were reported.
A trained weather spotter reported this wind gust.
Hail was reported on U.S. Highway 85, 5 miles south southeast of Brady.
Thunderstorm winds tore the porch roof off a lake residence at Brady Lake. The porch roof was tossed 60 to 70 feet. The time was estimated.
A wall cloud and golf ball size hail were reported.
Wind driven baseball size hail produced extensive damage in Melvin. Several residences reported their east facing windows were blown out.
An amateur radio operator reported roof damage to at least one residence near Melvin. The damage occurred just east of Ranch Road 2028, approximately 3 miles south of Melvin.
The public reported stripped corn crops.
Golf ball to tennis ball size hail was reported near the intersection of U.S. highway 190 and Ranch Road 1311.
Dime to nickel size hail covered the ground at the intersection of County Roads 216 and 218.
Strong thunderstorm winds broke four inch diameter tree limbs on the south side of Brady.
The public estimated a 60 MPH wind gust, 12 miles northeast of Brady.
A microburst in the Brady area resulted in five downed old power poles. This caused a power outage for much of McCulloch County that lasted approximately 18 hours.
The public reported quarter size hail at the corner of 7th and Cypress Street.

Strong thunderstorms winds estimated near 60 mph combined with large hail broke several of the northwest facing windows near the town of Voca. Exact hail size was unknown, but in concert with the wind, the hail must have been large to break glass.

Damaging thunderstorm winds peeled off the entire metal roof of the school located in Rochelle and damaged at least 15 other roofs in the area. Extensive water damage to the school was also reported. The winds downed many trees throughout the town.
The Automated Weather Observing System located at the Brady Airport measured a thunderstorm wind gust of 78 mph.
Damaging thunderstorm wind gusts of at least 60 mph knocked down Mesquite tree limbs that were four inches in diameter around Lohn.
Four to six inch diameter tree limbs were knocked down by the thunderstorm downburst on U.S. Highway 190.
A trained spotter reported four to six inch diameter tree limbs down by damaging thunderstorm winds at County Road 300 and FM 765.
A trained spotter reported damaging thunderstorm winds knocked down trees in and around Rochelle.

The Melvin postal worker reported damaging thunderstorm winds removed all of the roof decking from a residence, a hay barn was completely destroyed, a 100 year old oak tree was toppled, and two telephone poles were downed.
A trained spotter reported hen egg size hail on U.S. Highway 190.
A coop observer reported numerous power poles snapped at the base.
A coop observer reported a power pole snapped at the base on County Road 304.
The damaging thunderstorm winds were estimated at 60 mph and knocked down tree limbs and power lines.

A National Weather Service Damage Assessment Team found evidence of an EF1 Tornado that formed about 3 miles east northeast of Katemcy in northern Mason County and lifted about 2 miles north northwest of Fredonia in McCulloch County. The tornado mainly damaged a grove of trees sn…
Quarter to ping pong ball size hail was estimated by a member of the public.
Law enforcement officials reported quarter size hail along US Highway 87 about 3.5 miles south of Brady.
The public reported dime to nickel size hail about 3 miles southeast of Voca.
A trained spotter reported half dollar to hen egg size hail in Melvin. The large hail busted a windshield.
A trained spotter reported quarter to ping pong ball size hail in Melvin.
A trained spotter reported quarter size hail along US Highway 190 about 5 miles southwest of Brady.
Law enforcement reported numerous trees blown down across Brady.
A trained spotter reported mostly small hail covered the ground, with a few golf ball size hail stones.
A National Weather Service Damage Survey team determined an EF-2 tornado touched down about 8 miles southeast of Brady. Numerous hardwood trees were uprooted and many tree trunks were snapped off.
An amateur radio spotter reported quarter size hail.
A trained spotter reported lots of golf ball sized hail, along with pea size hail.
The report was relayed by an amateur radio operator.
An amateur radio operator reported penny size hail on the west side of Brady.

National Weather Service storm survey team found evidence of damage confirming an EFO tornado in Brady. Several trees lost limbs. One tree was uprooted, while another tree fell on a home. Some roof damage was also observed.
McCulloch County Sherrif's office reported quarter size hail just southwest of Brady.
Social media showed a picture of the quarter size hail near Early.
A picture from social media confirmed the quarter size hail.
Law Enforcement reported wind gusts of 60 mph.
Trained spotter reported and took a picture of this tornado in open country just east and northeast of Melvin. It was a brief touch down.

An EF-1 Tornado touched down near Highway 87 about a mile north of Melvin and continued northeast. It mostly uprooted large Oak Trees or snapped their trunks. It killed a calf and destroyed several |deer feeders. The tornado overturned a truck and cattle feeder. It damaged the la…
A 58 mph wind gust was measured at Curtis Field in Brady.
A trained spotter estimated baseball to possibly grapefruit size hail southwest of Voca at the intersection of County Roads 216 and 218. The time of this report was estimated using radar.
The windshield of a motor vehicle was destroyed.
Facebook photo of hail, with description saying that marble to baseball sized hail occurred near the intersection of County Road 330 and County Road 356 southeast of Doole.
A report on social media was received of pea to marble size hail in Brady.

Seven power poles were blown down near FM 503 and FM 504. Trees and brush had to be cleared from FM 503. The trained spotter reported everything was blown from west to east. Winds were estimated at 85 mph.
Damaging thunderstorm winds blew the roof off of a barn, uprooted a tree and broke large mesquite tree limbs.
Ping pong size hail and strong winds broke one window at the school in Lohn. The wind driven hail destroyed hundred acres of wheat between FM 504 and FM 765.
The combination of lots of hail and damaging thunderstorm winds resulted in near whiteout conditions for 5 minutes.
Three power poles were snapped about a mile south of FM 765 and US Highway 283 intersection.
Damaging thunderstorm winds destroyed a barn and threw it 300 feet to the east. |Four windows on the west side were broken by wind driven hail.
The public reported golf ball size hail in Melvin from social media.
The public reported half dollar to ping pong ball size hail near Lohn in northern Mcculloch County.
The public reported golf ball size hail just north of Brady.
Law Enforcement reported a large tree had fallen onto the road and required a wrecker to remove it.
The public reported a metal barn roof peeled off and a large pecan tree uprooted.
A storm chaser reported a wind gust of 70 mph 8 miles west-northwest of Brady.
Local Fire Department reported a metal outbuilding was destroyed.
There were trees blown down in the Pear Valley area off County Road 504.
There was lots of quarter size hail.
The hail likely melted a little bit, but near ping pong ball size hail.
There was half dollar size hail reported 1.5 miles southwest of Rochelle.
The Broadcast Media reported quarter to half dollar size hail on US 190, 4 miles east of Rochelle.
The public reported half dollar size hail.
The public reported golf ball size hail 2 miles west-southwest of Placid.

The public reported hen egg size hail 2 miles north of Salt Gap.
The public reported tennis ball size hail 2 miles north of Salt Gap.

A Storm Chaser reported baseball size hail 7 miles northwest of Brady.

The public reported tennis ball size hail in Brady.

Fire department reported 2 electrical power poles broken and roof damage with tin sheets blown off part of a house.
Public reported nickel to quarter size hail in Melvin. Also, over 1 inch of rainfall with this storm.
A NWS spotter reported nickel to quarter size hail.
A brief tornado touched down near a residence off Private Road 839 in McCulloch County and lifted a large metal barn into the air which landed on a neighbor's barn along their property line.
Public reported a large tree branch snapped by strong winds in Melvin.
Public reported half dollar size hail.

The public reported baseball size hail in Voca.
The public reported tennis ball size hail 5 miles west-southwest of Voca.
The public measured larger than 3 inch diameter hail 5 miles west-northwest of Katemcy.
Law enforcement reported the Lohn ISD school roof got blown off by wind and is in the middle of the street just east of FM2635.
Public reported 1 inch tree limbs broken and shingles blown off.
An automated weather observation station at the Brady Municipal Airport measured a 63 mph wind gust.
Public reported ping pong ball size hail.
A trained spotter reported 65 to 70 mph wind gusts that were fairly steady on CR216 just south of CR218.
The Fire Department reported baseball size hail 2 miles southeast of Voca. Also, power lines were snapped and large oak trees were blown down.
A trained spotter reported golf ball size breaking windows to a house. The hail was possibly larger up to tennis ball size hail. Time based on radar.
A trained spotter reported wind gusts of 60 to 70 mph. Time based on radar.
A trained spotter reported golf ball to tennis ball size hail that started breaking her windows while on the phone. Time based on radar.
A trained spotter reported baseball size hail in Voca.
Trained spotter reported numerous windows broken by strong winds and hail.
Public reported 1 inch tree limbs broken and shingles blown off.
An automated weather observation station at Brady Municipal Airport measured a 63 mph wind gust.
